LiPD and Neotoma interoperability

lipdR authors

2026-11-09

Source: vignettes/lipd2neotoma.Rmd
lipd2neotoma.Rmd

lipdR can convert between the LiPD and Neotoma ecosystems in both directions. This makes it possible to pull records out of the Neotoma Paleoecology Database, work with them using the LiPD tools, and push results back.

The conversion functions require the suggested package neotoma2 (available on CRAN) and, for spatial handling, sf:

install.packages(c("neotoma2", "sf"))

The code chunks below are not evaluated when the vignette is built, because they make live calls to the Neotoma API.

Neotoma to LiPD

Download a site from Neotoma and convert it into a LiPD object with neotoma2lipd():

library(lipdR)

# Retrieve a site and its data from Neotoma
sites <- neotoma2::get_sites(sitename = "Bambili 2")
downloads <- neotoma2::get_downloads(sites)

# Convert to a LiPD object
L <- neotoma2lipd(downloads)

summary(L)

The resulting object is a standard LiPD object: it can be validated, written to a .lpd file, flattened to a time series, and passed to the rest of the ecosystem (geoChronR, actR, compositeR, and so on).

validLipd(L)
ts <- extractTs(L)
writeLipd(L, "~/Downloads/")

LiPD to Neotoma

The reverse conversion, lipd2neotoma(), builds a Neotoma site object from a LiPD object:

L <- readLipd("path/to/a/file.lpd")

site <- lipd2neotoma(L)

# The result is a neotoma2 'site' object
neotoma2::samples(site)

Round-tripping

Because both directions are supported, a LiPD object can be pushed to Neotoma and back:

site <- lipd2neotoma(L)
L2   <- neotoma2lipd(site)

Core metadata (coordinates, publications, measurement data) is preserved across the round-trip, though the two data models are not identical, so some ecosystem-specific fields may not survive.
